problem.name: Normalized trace estimation for a quantum circuit
problem.name_latex: Normalized trace estimation for a quantum circuit
problem.statement_latex: Given an $n$-qubit unitary circuit $U$ of size $g$, estimate both components of $2^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}(U)$ to additive error $\varepsilon$ with failure probability $\delta$. The input is a succinct circuit. Complexity uses gates and classical time; the problem characterizes DQC1.
problem.statement_text: Given an $n$-qubit unitary circuit $U$ of size $g$, estimate both components of $2^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}(U)$ to additive error $\varepsilon$ with failure probability $\delta$. The input is a succinct circuit. Complexity uses gates and classical time; the problem characterizes DQC1.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial quantum gates versus the best applicable exponential or subexponential generic classical trace computation.
strength.description_text: Polynomial quantum gates versus the best applicable exponential or subexponential generic classical trace computation.

evidence.description_latex: Inverse-polynomial-accuracy trace estimation is DQC1-complete; efficient classical estimation would simulate DQC1.
evidence.description_text: Inverse-polynomial-accuracy trace estimation is DQC1-complete; efficient classical estimation would simulate DQC1.

hardware.description_latex: One clean and $n$ maximally mixed qubits plus controlled-circuit workspace; repetitions scale as $\varepsilon^{-2}$.
hardware.description_text: One clean and $n$ maximally mixed qubits plus controlled-circuit workspace; repetitions scale as $\varepsilon^{-2}$.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(g\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))$ gates by Knill--Laflamme. A clean control applies controlled-$U$ to $I/2^n$; its $X$ and $Y$ expectations give the trace.
quantum.headline_text: $O(g\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))$ gates by Knill–Laflamme. A clean control applies controlled-$U$ to $I/2^n$; its $X$ and $Y$ expectations give the trace.

classical.headline_latex: Random-vector trace estimation with state-vector circuit application costs $O(g2^n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))$. Tensor contraction provides width-dependent alternatives. For fixed finite algebraic gates, trace path counting also costs $\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}$ in the size $s$ of its sparse Boolean encoding.
